title: TT-Bio benchmarks: biomolecular structure prediction, design and binding affinity on Tenstorrent hardware
subtitle: Eight structure-prediction models, two binder-design models and one binding-affinity model at 512 residues, measured on Tenstorrent Blackhole and on NVIDIA H200, B200 and A100.
notes: This file is the only place numbers are edited. index.html reads it and derives everything else.
Never write a derived value here. Server throughput, cost per hour and both throughput-per-dollar charts are computed in the page from s_per_fold, accelerators, price and power.

A row is published only when every processor column is measured. A model with a blank column waits in perf/page_rows_pending.json until its missing cells exist, because a half-measured row still draws a bar and reads as a claim. scripts/site_publish_guard.py enforces this, --strip holds a row and --restore publishes it.

One cell per model per platform. A Tenstorrent cell is tt-bio main in its default mode, with its --fast run kept beside it under `fast`; an NVIDIA cell is the Anthropic kit's exact mode where the kit has the model (ref "kit") and the authors' own release where it does not (ref "stock"), with the other runs kept as `fast` and `stock`. Every Tenstorrent cell states its accuracy from the release gate (perf/bmk/gate_parity.py). Numbers come from state/bmk/BOARD.md through perf/bmk/board_to_page.py. A cell with no measurement gets a status and a reason, never an estimate.

The A100 appears twice: as a card, and as the DGX A100 640GB, the eight-GPU box NVIDIA sold that card in. The $175,000 that box carries is an assumed street price, not a vendor list price, and it is labelled as one everywhere it is used.
A design model carrying 'hidden': true keeps every measured cell here and is drawn nowhere. Delete that one line to publish the row again.

Every Tenstorrent cell states the board it was measured on. It inherits `measured_on` from its platform and overrides it only if it ran somewhere else. The column is priced as a p150a; the board that produced the number is a separate fact and is stated as one.

The embed block is measured but not published. All six rows carry "hidden": true and the page has no code that reads it, so the guard counts them out of the title, the subtitle and the meta description. site/README.md records what was run. Restoring the section means dropping the flags, putting the chart and the t-embed table back, and moving EXPECT_ROWS.embed in render_check.js in the same commit.

scope.description: CDK2 (PDB 1HCL) tandem-duplicated to 512 residues, one protein chain, no ligands, a fixed 35-sequence MSA.
scope.protocol: Warm runs, one prediction at a time on one accelerator, the same two input files on every platform, each model at its own shipped recycle and sampling-step settings. Each Tenstorrent cell is tt-bio main in its default mode.
scope.nvidia_code: An NVIDIA cell is one of two things, and the per-GPU list at the end of this entry says which. A kit cell is Anthropic's open kit for these models (github.com/anthropics/uplifting-biomolecular-modeling, commit f4f62fa65) in its exact mode: the authors' upstream package, patched in memory with fused kernels and CUDA graphs that keep its arithmetic. A stock cell is the authors' own release with nothing added. Neither is NVIDIA BioNeMo or a NIM. Each kit cell's machine also timed the kit's fast mode, which gives up bit-for-bit agreement for speed, and the unpatched upstream package; both are in the hover text and the data file, not on the bars. The kit does not carry BoltzGen or Nesso-1, so those are stock on every GPU. On the B200, three of the kit's RoseTTAFold3 kernels do not run and are switched off with the kit's own setting, and PXDesign runs without its fused LayerNorm, which has no B200 build.
scope.nvidia_impl: Exact mode was checked rather than assumed. With determinism switched on, OpenFold3, Protenix-v2 and both ESMFold2 rows returned the same coordinates as the unpatched package bit for bit on the A100, the H200 and the B200, and so did OpenDDE. The kit has no deterministic switch for RoseTTAFold3; it still matched bit for bit on 8 of 10 A100 folds, and on the H200 and the B200 it sat a median 0.57 Å and 0.19 Å from the unpatched package. Boltz-2 has no deterministic recipe in exact mode, and the kit runs OpenBind-0 from a bf16 configuration where upstream ships fp32. For both, on every GPU, the median distance between the kit's structure and the unpatched package's is smaller than the median distance between two runs of the unpatched package. PXDesign's designs sit a median 0.014 Å from the unpatched package's on the A100, 0.005 Å on the H200 and 0.001 Å on the B200.
scope.timed_region: Each cell times what that platform's own harness times, and the regions are not identical. Every Tenstorrent number is a whole prediction or design call, with featurisation and file writing inside it. A kit cell for Boltz-2, OpenFold3, OpenBind-0, Protenix-v2, OpenDDE or PXDesign times the model call alone and leaves host featurisation outside the timer, which makes those ratios larger than a like-for-like comparison would. An ESMFold2 kit cell times the fold call, sequence in and structure out. A RoseTTAFold3 cell times a whole fold on both sides. A cell measured before this campaign describes its own timer in its hover text.

cost_model.amortisation_basis: Four years is this page's assumption for how long an AI accelerator earns its keep: one year shorter than the general-purpose server life Amazon reports in its 10-Q, because an accelerator generation lasts about two years. A shorter window favours the cheaper box, so the range below brackets it.
cost_model.utilisation: The machine predicts continuously, so every hour of ownership is an hour of throughput.
cost_model.formula: Throughput per dollar, with the DGX H200 set to 1.00x, on two bases. Purchase price: predictions per hour / price, with no amortisation window, because the window cancels from that ratio. Total cost of ownership: predictions per hour / cost per hour, where cost per hour = price / (4 x 8766 h) + power kW x $/kWh.

design.cond: Wall-clock seconds to return one binder design on a single AI Processor, warm, at the model's shipped defaults. Shorter is better. Every platform runs one design at a time, the same protocol as the prediction rows.
design.note: One design at a time on every platform, so nothing here compares a batch against a single. The two rows run different targets at different sizes and are not comparable to each other: BoltzGen at 514 tokens, PXDesign at 592. BoltzGen's size is a ceiling as well as a choice, because the next size up overflows L1 on the Blackhole AI Processor measured here, and a larger target would work the GPUs harder, so read that row as the most favourable honest reading rather than a limit. No size ceiling has been measured for PXDesign. Batching is the one lever these rows leave out; the PXDesign row note says how much it moves each side.
design.methods: One pinned target per row at that model's shipped defaults, one design at a time on every platform: BoltzGen at 500 sampling steps, PXDesign at 400. The PXDesign row times its generator, which is what the CLI returns; the filtering pipeline upstream runs after it is not on the CLI and is not in the cell. The row note says which steps each side's timer covers. Tenstorrent figures are warm medians of four designs on one Blackhole AI Processor, with the cold design dropped, and for BoltzGen also the one that pays the checkpoint switch. GPU figures come from the same protocol on rented single-GPU nodes. Designs are validated per run rather than digested: chain sizes, residue topology and finite coordinates, never atom equality between siblings, because sibling designs legitimately differ.

models.server_charts_note: RFdiffusion3 is not on the per-server or per-dollar charts. Those charts scale seconds per job by accelerator count, and this row's two sides do not have the same lever: a batch of eight is worth 2.12x on the H200, 2.50x on the B200 and 1.79x on the A100, measured at shipped defaults with the H200 at 79 % of its 700 W and 98 % utilisation, while the Blackhole AI Processor gains 1.04x at 3844 atoms and does not fit a batch of eight. At batch 1 the Galaxy reads 1.20x a DGX H200; at each side's best batch it reads 0.57x, so the batch decides the sign rather than the size. The seconds chart keeps the row, because one at a time is the right protocol for latency. BoltzGen stays on both charts: its batched path drifts 0.5-2.8 A per slot, which makes a batched design a different design, so batch 1 is the production configuration on the GPU as well as here.

models.name: PXDesign
models.target: beta-galactosidase (1DP0 chain A) cropped to 512 residues around one fixed epitope, 80-residue binder, 592 tokens
models.note: This row is what `tt-bio design --model pxdesign` returns: the PXDesign-d generator, which writes a binder backbone with no sequence. The filtering pipeline upstream runs after it (ProteinMPNN, AF2-IG and a Protenix filter) is not on the CLI and not in the cell. The Tenstorrent cell times featurisation, generation and the CIF write; a kit cell times generation alone, which favours the NVIDIA column. The LacZ crop is a cost fixture, right for seconds and wrong for design quality, because its epitope is an arbitrary exposed loop. Batching is the lever this protocol leaves out, and it helps the GPUs more than the Blackhole AI Processor. Upstream recommends thousands of designs per target, so for a real campaign the batched rate matters more than the one-design latency shown here.

affinity.cond: Wall-clock seconds to return one binding-affinity prediction on a single AI Processor, warm, at the shipped defaults. Shorter is better. One prediction at a time on every platform.
affinity.note: Nesso-1 returns eleven scalars and no coordinates, so it cannot run the CDK2 fixture the fold rows use: it conditions on ESM-2 embeddings rather than an MSA and it needs a ligand. This row is measured on the 512 aa rung of the port's own size ladder instead, 532 tokens, one protein and one ligand. Read it against the other rows for what a 512-residue input costs on each platform, not as the same computation.
affinity.methods: One protein plus one ligand at the shipped defaults: bf16 trunk, fp32 affinity stacks, 5 recycling steps, 256-token pocket crop, one prediction at a time. The Tenstorrent figure is the warm median of four predictions on one Blackhole AI Processor with the model resident, each one preparing its input (parse, RDKit conformer, ESM-2) and then predicting. Every GPU figure times one call of upstream's Lightning predict loop per prediction, data loader and output writer included, with the RDKit conformer and ESM-2 run once beforehand and left outside. On the A100 the predict step inside that call is 1.84 s, so most of the GPU figure is host work.

embed.methods: Six encoders at the shipped defaults, --fast off, mean pooling, no masked-LM logits. bfloat16 on both sides. attn_implementation sdpa is requested on the NVIDIA side and the harness counts the calls rather than trusting the flag. The input is one 512-residue sequence from scripts/gpu_vs_tt/fixtures/prot512.seq (sha256 141f7d47...), copied to fill the batch; both sides assert that digest before timing. Tenstorrent figures are warm medians of n=7 on one Blackhole AI Processor under benchlock with the loadavg recorded; NVIDIA figures are warm medians of n=15 on rented single-GPU nodes with the cold rep discarded. Every cell carries its own accuracy check: on Tenstorrent an all-finite pooled digest with the batch rows asserted identical, on NVIDIA the cosine of the bf16 output against an fp32 recomputation of the same forward, 0.999956 to 0.999996 against a 0.999 bar.

models.name: SaProt 35M
models.note: At 16.6 seq/s this row is slower than SaProt 1.3B at 23.4 on the same card, which reads as a page bug and is not one. SaProt 35M has a head dim of 24 (hidden 480 over 20 heads), neither tile-aligned nor aligned with the fused on-device rotary kernel, so the port splits heads, applies RoPE on host in fp32 and pads 24 to 32 on host, once per layer. That costs 35.2 ms per layer against 4.5-4.7 ms per layer for the two larger sizes at hidden 1280, and it is also why this is the widest-spread Tenstorrent row here at 13.0 %. Documented in docs/saprot-parity.md under "35M host-side RoPE path"; a fix is proposed, not landed.

tt-galaxy.label: Tenstorrent, Galaxy
tt-galaxy.detail: Galaxy Blackhole starting at $160,000: 6U air-cooled, 32x Blackhole ASIC, 1 TB GDDR6 at 16 TB/s, power 8 to 10 kW average and 12 kW maximum; this page uses the 12 kW maximum.

tt-cards.label: Tenstorrent, Blackhole cards
tt-cards.detail: Blackhole p150a $1,399 list, 120 Tensix cores, 32 GB GDDR6 at 512 GB/s, 300 W.

dgx-h200.label: NVIDIA DGX H100/H200 User Guide
dgx-h200.detail: 8x H200 with 1,128 GB total GPU memory, 10.2 kW maximum system power.

dgx-b200.label: NVIDIA DGX B200
dgx-b200.detail: 8x Blackwell GPU, 1,440 GB HBM3e, system power usage ~14.3 kW max. NVIDIA posts no price.

dgx-a100.label: NVIDIA DGX A100 datasheet
dgx-a100.detail: The 640GB configuration: 8x NVIDIA A100 80GB Tensor Core GPUs, 640 GB total GPU memory, 6 NVSwitches, 6.5 kW maximum system power, dual AMD Rome 7742, 2 TB system memory, 6U. NVIDIA's DGX A100 user guide gives the same 6.5 kW. The 320GB configuration is the same chassis with 40 GB GPUs; this page describes the 640GB one, because the A100 SXM4 80 GB it measured is the card that box carries.

dgx-a100-price.label: DGX A100 price: an assumption, not a source
dgx-a100-price.detail: $175,000 is what this page assumes a DGX A100 640GB costs. Moritz Thuning supplied it on 2026-08-16. NVIDIA does not post DGX pricing and published no list price for this system, and no vendor quote is cited for it, so it is the one price here that is not a published figure. Every DGX A100 cost bar rests on it.

eia-industrial.label: US EIA, Electric Power Monthly, table 5.3
eia-industrial.detail: US average retail price of electricity to the industrial sector, 9.77 cents/kWh for July 2026, released 2026-09-24. The commercial-sector price for the same month is 14.53 cents/kWh and is used in the sensitivity check.

amzn-10q.label: Amazon, Form 10-Q, useful life of servers
amzn-10q.detail: From 1 January 2025 Amazon depreciates a subset of its servers and networking equipment over five years, down from six, citing the pace of AI hardware development. This page's four-year window is one year shorter than that.

broadberry-dgx-h200.label: Broadberry, NVIDIA DGX H200
broadberry-dgx-h200.detail: $467,311.30 excluding sales tax for the base configuration with 3 years of NVIDIA support and installation, against a stated RRP of $584,139.13. NVIDIA publishes no DGX price, so this page uses what a US buyer is quoted.

broadberry-dgx-b200.label: Broadberry, NVIDIA DGX B200
broadberry-dgx-b200.detail: $562,154.09 excluding sales tax for the base configuration with 3 years of NVIDIA support and installation, against a stated RRP of $702,692.62. NVIDIA publishes no DGX price, so this page uses what a US buyer is quoted.

caveats: Rows are not a cross-model ranking. Boltz-2 and OpenFold3 do 3 recycles where ESMFold2, Protenix-v2 and OpenDDE do 10, because that is what each ships. Compare a model to itself across hardware. BoltzGen returns a binder design, not a prediction; its bars share an axis with the prediction models but not a unit.

The NVIDIA cells were measured on 14 and 15 October 2026 on rented single-GPU nodes, the A100s with AMD EPYC 7513 hosts, the H200 with an Intel Xeon Platinum 8568Y+ and the B200 with an Intel Xeon Platinum 8559C. The host matters for the dispatch-bound trunks and is not corrected for.

RoseTTAFold3's NVIDIA cells carry the widest spreads on this page, and host featurisation is why: host prep varies far more run to run than device work does. Its nine H200 folds span 11.81 to 14.16 s, where Boltz-2's four span 4.105 to 4.118 s.

The NVIDIA cells do not share one software stack. Each kit pins its own torch and CUDA per model, and a stock cell runs what its authors pin; every cell's hover text names its versions and driver. That is one more reason to compare a model to itself across hardware rather than rows against each other.
